question.text: What two things make you a Michigan resident?

answer.text: To count as a Michigan resident, you have to live in Michigan and have shown that you are legally present in the state.

teaching.text: Residency needs both parts together: living in Michigan and having shown legal presence. Remember: live here, prove legal presence.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To count as a Michigan resident, you have to live in Michigan and have shown that you are legally present in the state.

question.text: Can the Secretary of State issue an original license or ID to someone who is not a legal Michigan resident?

answer.text: State law bars the Secretary of State from issuing an original driver’s license or state ID card to anyone who is not a legal Michigan resident.

teaching.text: Only legal residents can get an original Michigan license or state ID, so residency always comes first. Remember: no residency, no original card.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: State law bars the Secretary of State from issuing an original driver’s license or state ID card to anyone who is not a legal Michigan resident.

question.text: When must a new resident title and register their vehicle, and what do they hand in?

answer.text: A new resident must title and register their vehicle at a Secretary of State office right away, handing in the title or ownership proof from the former home state.

teaching.text: The vehicle has no waiting period: title and register it at a Secretary of State office right away. Remember: vehicle paperwork right away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A new resident must title and register their vehicle at a Secretary of State office right away, handing in the title or ownership proof from the former home state.

question.text: How long can a new resident keep using their out-of-state license?

answer.text: A driver’s license or state ID from another state may be used until your Michigan residency is established, and after that you apply for the Michigan card at a Secretary of State office.

teaching.text: Your old license keeps working while you establish residency, and then you apply for the Michigan card. Remember: old license until residency.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver’s license or state ID from another state may be used until your Michigan residency is established, and after that you apply for the Michigan card at a Secretary of State office.

question.text: What happens to your driving record from your former state?

answer.text: Michigan requests your driving record from your former home state, and that record becomes part of your Michigan driving record.

teaching.text: Moving does not wipe your history; your former state's record becomes part of your Michigan record. Remember: your old record follows you.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Michigan requests your driving record from your former home state, and that record becomes part of your Michigan driving record.

question.text: What must you do first if your out-of-state license is suspended or revoked?

answer.text: If your out-of-state license is suspended or revoked, you must settle the open issues with that former state before Michigan will accept your license application.

teaching.text: A suspension or revocation in your old state must be settled there before Michigan accepts your application. Remember: settle old state first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your out-of-state license is suspended or revoked, you must settle the open issues with that former state before Michigan will accept your license application.

question.text: What happens to your out-of-state license once your Michigan application is accepted, and why?

answer.text: Once your Michigan application is accepted, the out-of-state license is invalidated and handed back, because Michigan lets a driver hold only one valid license at a time.

teaching.text: Michigan allows only one valid license, so the old card is invalidated and handed back at acceptance. Remember: one valid license only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once your Michigan application is accepted, the out-of-state license is invalidated and handed back, because Michigan lets a driver hold only one valid license at a time.

question.text: At what moment does an out-of-state license stop being valid for a new resident?

answer.text: An out-of-state license stays usable only until Michigan residency is established, and it is invalidated at the moment the Michigan application is accepted, not when the new card arrives.

teaching.text: The old license ends when Michigan accepts the application, not when the new card arrives. Remember: accepted application ends it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An out-of-state license stays usable only until Michigan residency is established, and it is invalidated at the moment the Michigan application is accepted, not when the new card arrives.

question.text: How does the timing for vehicle paperwork differ from the timing for the license?

answer.text: Vehicle title and registration must be done immediately by a new resident, whereas the driver’s license application waits until residency is established.

teaching.text: Vehicle paperwork happens right away, but the license application waits for residency. Remember: car now, license later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Vehicle title and registration must be done immediately by a new resident, whereas the driver’s license application waits until residency is established.

question.text: When is someone who has never held a license refused a Michigan license because of convictions?

answer.text: Someone who has never held a license from any state or country is refused a Michigan license when their record shows two or more moving-violation convictions within three years of the application date.

teaching.text: A never-licensed applicant with two or more moving-violation convictions in three years is refused. Remember: never licensed, two strikes refused.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Someone who has never held a license from any state or country is refused a Michigan license when their record shows two or more moving-violation convictions within three years of the application date.

question.text: How many convictions may your record carry in the three years before you apply?

answer.text: To apply for a license, your driving record may carry no more than one conviction within the three years before you apply.

teaching.text: Every applicant may carry at most one conviction in the three years before applying. Remember: one conviction maximum.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To apply for a license, your driving record may carry no more than one conviction within the three years before you apply.

question.text: How do the two conviction rules for license applicants differ?

answer.text: The two conviction rules differ: a never-licensed applicant is refused at two or more moving-violation convictions in three years, while any applicant may carry at most one conviction in the three years before applying.

teaching.text: Two or more moving violations refuses a never-licensed applicant, while one conviction is the general limit. Remember: two refuses, one allowed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The two conviction rules differ: a never-licensed applicant is refused at two or more moving-violation convictions in three years, while any applicant may carry at most one conviction in the three years before applying.

question.text: What makes licensing requirements differ, and what can specialized licenses add?

answer.text: Licensing requirements differ by license type, group designator and endorsement, and specialized licenses such as a chauffeur’s license or a commercial driver’s license may add testing and a background check.

teaching.text: Each license type, group designator and endorsement has its own requirements, and specialized licenses may add tests and a background check. Remember: type, group, endorsement decide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Licensing requirements differ by license type, group designator and endorsement, and specialized licenses such as a chauffeur’s license or a commercial driver’s license may add testing and a background check.

question.text: What is Michigan's basic driver's license called?

answer.text: The operator’s license is Michigan’s basic driver’s license.

teaching.text: When you hear operator's license, think of the basic, everyday Michigan license. Remember: operator means basic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The operator’s license is Michigan’s basic driver’s license.

question.text: What does a chauffeur's license require, and when do you need one?

answer.text: A chauffeur’s license needs a minimum age of sixteen and a passed written chauffeur’s test, and it is required when your job is mainly driving a vehicle rated ten thousand pounds GVWR or more, carrying passengers or property for hire, or driving a bus or school bus.

teaching.text: The chauffeur's license is about driving as your job, including vehicles rated ten thousand pounds or more, hire, and buses. Remember: driving for work or hire.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A chauffeur’s license needs a minimum age of sixteen and a passed written chauffeur’s test, and it is required when your job is mainly driving a vehicle rated ten thousand pounds GVWR or more, carrying passengers or property for hire, or driving a bus or school bus.

question.text: Which vehicles or loads require a commercial driver's license?

answer.text: A commercial driver’s license is required for a single vehicle rated twenty-six thousand one pounds GVWR or more, a combination towing ten thousand one pounds or more when the GCWR is twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, a vehicle built to carry sixteen or more people counting the driver, or placarded hazardous materials.

teaching.text: Commercial licenses cover the heaviest vehicles, big passenger loads and placarded hazardous materials. Remember: heavy, many riders, hazmat.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A commercial driver’s license is required for a single vehicle rated twenty-six thousand one pounds GVWR or more, a combination towing ten thousand one pounds or more when the GCWR is twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, a vehicle built to carry sixteen or more people counting the driver, or placarded hazardous materials.

question.text: What age and record rules apply to commercial drivers, and what changes at twenty-one?

answer.text: Commercial drivers must be at least eighteen and suspension-free for the thirty-six months before applying; drivers aged eighteen to twenty-one may drive commercially only inside Michigan, and age twenty-one is needed to cross state lines or haul placarded hazardous materials.

teaching.text: Commercial drivers start at eighteen inside Michigan and need twenty-one to cross state lines or haul hazardous materials. Remember: eighteen in state, twenty-one across.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Commercial drivers must be at least eighteen and suspension-free for the thirty-six months before applying; drivers aged eighteen to twenty-one may drive commercially only inside Michigan, and age twenty-one is needed to cross state lines or haul placarded hazardous materials.

question.text: How do the chauffeur's and commercial license weight thresholds differ?

answer.text: The chauffeur’s license threshold is a vehicle rated ten thousand pounds GVWR driven mainly for work, while the commercial license threshold for a single vehicle is twenty-six thousand one pounds GVWR.

teaching.text: Ten thousand pounds driven for work points to a chauffeur's license; twenty-six thousand one pounds points to commercial. Remember: ten thousand versus twenty-six thousand one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The chauffeur’s license threshold is a vehicle rated ten thousand pounds GVWR driven mainly for work, while the commercial license threshold for a single vehicle is twenty-six thousand one pounds GVWR.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: ten thousand versus twenty-six thousand one

question.text: What can a commercial driver do at eighteen versus at twenty-one?

answer.text: Age eighteen lets a commercial driver operate only inside Michigan, while age twenty-one is the line for crossing state lines or hauling placarded hazardous materials.

teaching.text: At eighteen a commercial driver stays in Michigan; at twenty-one they may cross state lines or haul hazmat. Remember: eighteen in state only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Age eighteen lets a commercial driver operate only inside Michigan, while age twenty-one is the line for crossing state lines or hauling placarded hazardous materials.

question.text: Do you need a moped license if you already hold a valid operator's or chauffeur's license?

answer.text: A valid operator’s or chauffeur’s license already covers riding a moped, but a suspended, revoked or denied license makes you ineligible for a moped license.

teaching.text: A valid operator's or chauffeur's license already covers mopeds, but a suspended or denied license blocks a moped license. Remember: license covers the moped.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A valid operator’s or chauffeur’s license already covers riding a moped, but a suspended, revoked or denied license makes you ineligible for a moped license.

question.text: Who may apply for a moped license without a driver's license, and what tests are taken?

answer.text: An unlicensed teen age fifteen or older with a parent’s approval may apply for a moped license and must take vision, written knowledge and traffic sign tests.

teaching.text: Unlicensed teens fifteen and older need a parent's approval plus vision, knowledge and sign tests. Remember: fifteen plus parent plus tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An unlicensed teen age fifteen or older with a parent’s approval may apply for a moped license and must take vision, written knowledge and traffic sign tests.

question.text: What are the two ways to earn a CY motorcycle endorsement, and who must take the course?

answer.text: A CY motorcycle endorsement requires either a rider education course or the written knowledge test plus a motorcycle skills test, and the course is mandatory for riders aged sixteen to seventeen and for adults who fail the skills test twice.

teaching.text: Most adults may choose the course or the tests, but the course is required at sixteen and seventeen and after two failed skills tests. Remember: course or tests to ride.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A CY motorcycle endorsement requires either a rider education course or the written knowledge test plus a motorcycle skills test, and the course is mandatory for riders aged sixteen to seventeen and for adults who fail the skills test twice.

question.text: What does the CY three W restriction allow, and how is it earned?

answer.text: A CY 3W restriction limits a rider to three-wheeled motorcycles and is earned through a three-wheeled safety course or the written test plus a three-wheel skills test.

teaching.text: The three W restriction narrows you to three-wheeled motorcycles, earned by a three-wheel course or tests. Remember: three wheels only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A CY 3W restriction limits a rider to three-wheeled motorcycles and is earned through a three-wheeled safety course or the written test plus a three-wheel skills test.

question.text: What setup does the recreational double R endorsement cover?

answer.text: The recreational double R endorsement, which requires a knowledge test, covers a pickup pulling a fifth-wheel recreational trailer with a second trailer hitched behind it.

teaching.text: Double R is the endorsement for a pickup towing a fifth wheel with a second trailer behind it. Remember: fifth wheel plus one more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The recreational double R endorsement, which requires a knowledge test, covers a pickup pulling a fifth-wheel recreational trailer with a second trailer hitched behind it.

question.text: What does the farmer endorsement let farm operations do?

answer.text: The farmer endorsement lets farm operations move equipment, livestock and produce, and it may call for a general knowledge test and a combination vehicles test.

teaching.text: The farmer endorsement is for farm operations moving equipment, livestock and produce. Remember: farm loads on the road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The farmer endorsement lets farm operations move equipment, livestock and produce, and it may call for a general knowledge test and a combination vehicles test.

question.text: How do moped rules differ for a licensed driver and an unlicensed teen?

answer.text: A licensed driver needs no moped license at all, while an unlicensed teen needs to be at least fifteen, have parental approval, and pass vision, knowledge and sign tests.

teaching.text: Licensed drivers skip the moped license, while unlicensed teens need age fifteen, a parent and three tests. Remember: licensed skip it, teens test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A licensed driver needs no moped license at all, while an unlicensed teen needs to be at least fifteen, have parental approval, and pass vision, knowledge and sign tests.

question.text: How does the full CY endorsement differ from the CY three W restriction?

answer.text: The full CY endorsement covers motorcycles in general, while the CY 3W restriction limits the rider to three-wheeled motorcycles only.

teaching.text: CY covers motorcycles in general, while CY three W covers only three-wheeled motorcycles. Remember: CY all, three W trikes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The full CY endorsement covers motorcycles in general, while the CY 3W restriction limits the rider to three-wheeled motorcycles only.

question.text: When is rider education mandatory instead of optional?

answer.text: Rider education is optional for most adults but mandatory for riders aged sixteen to seventeen and for adults after a second failed motorcycle skills test.

teaching.text: The rider course is a choice for most adults, but required at sixteen and seventeen and after a second failed skills test. Remember: young riders and repeat failures.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Rider education is optional for most adults but mandatory for riders aged sixteen to seventeen and for adults after a second failed motorcycle skills test.

question.text: What does an enhanced driver's license let you do at the border?

answer.text: An enhanced driver’s license lets you come back into the United States from Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean, by land or by sea, with no other identity papers, and enhanced cards are also REAL ID compliant.

teaching.text: The enhanced card handles land and sea re-entry from nearby countries and also counts as REAL ID. Remember: enhanced card crosses back home.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An enhanced driver’s license lets you come back into the United States from Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean, by land or by sea, with no other identity papers, and enhanced cards are also REAL ID compliant.

question.text: Starting in May of twenty twenty-five, what do you need a REAL ID-compliant document for?

answer.text: Starting May seven, two thousand twenty-five, Michigan residents need a REAL ID-compliant document to board a domestic flight or to enter certain federal facilities, military bases and nuclear power plants.

teaching.text: REAL ID matters for domestic flights and certain federal sites, starting May seventh, twenty twenty-five. Remember: flights and federal sites.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Starting May seven, two thousand twenty-five, Michigan residents need a REAL ID-compliant document to board a domestic flight or to enter certain federal facilities, military bases and nuclear power plants.

question.text: Which documents count as REAL ID-compliant?

answer.text: REAL ID-compliant documents include licenses and IDs from states meeting the federal standard and valid U.S. passports and passport cards, and the TSA lists acceptable documents at tsa.gov.

teaching.text: Compliant state cards, valid passports and passport cards all count, and the TSA keeps the full list. Remember: compliant state card or passport.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: REAL ID-compliant documents include licenses and IDs from states meeting the federal standard and valid U.S. passports and passport cards, and the TSA lists acceptable documents at tsa.gov.

question.text: How can you tell a Michigan card is REAL ID compliant?

answer.text: A Michigan card is REAL ID compliant when its upper right corner shows a star in a gold circle or a star inside a Michigan outline, and enhanced cards without a star still comply and receive the star at renewal or replacement.

teaching.text: Check the upper right corner for a star in a gold circle or inside a Michigan outline. Remember: look for the star.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Michigan card is REAL ID compliant when its upper right corner shows a star in a gold circle or a star inside a Michigan outline, and enhanced cards without a star still comply and receive the star at renewal or replacement.

question.text: Is REAL ID required for everyone?

answer.text: REAL ID is optional, and you may not need it if you neither fly nor plan to enter those federal sites, or if you hold an acceptable alternative such as a valid U.S. passport.

teaching.text: If you never fly and never visit those federal sites, or you have a passport, REAL ID is optional. Remember: optional if you never need it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: REAL ID is optional, and you may not need it if you neither fly nor plan to enter those federal sites, or if you hold an acceptable alternative such as a valid U.S. passport.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: optional if you never need it

question.text: What does adding REAL ID cost at renewal compared with other times?

answer.text: Adding REAL ID costs nothing extra when you renew, but applying for it at any other time means paying the duplicate card fee.

teaching.text: Renewal is the free time to add REAL ID; any other time costs the duplicate card fee. Remember: free at renewal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Adding REAL ID costs nothing extra when you renew, but applying for it at any other time means paying the duplicate card fee.

question.text: What is a standard card without REAL ID marked, and what can it still be used for?

answer.text: A standard card without REAL ID is marked “Not for Federal Identification” yet still works for driving and as identification for cashing checks, renting vehicles, buying age-restricted items and entering casinos.

teaching.text: A standard card says Not for Federal Identification but still works for driving and everyday ID. Remember: standard still drives and identifies.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A standard card without REAL ID is marked “Not for Federal Identification” yet still works for driving and as identification for cashing checks, renting vehicles, buying age-restricted items and entering casinos.

question.text: Which is REAL ID compliant: an enhanced card without a star or a standard card marked Not for Federal Identification?

answer.text: An enhanced card without a star is already REAL ID compliant, while a standard card marked Not for Federal Identification is not, even though both remain valid for driving.

teaching.text: An enhanced card without a star still complies; a standard card does not, though both let you drive. Remember: enhanced counts, standard does not.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An enhanced card without a star is already REAL ID compliant, while a standard card marked Not for Federal Identification is not, even though both remain valid for driving.

question.text: When does asking for REAL ID trigger a fee?

answer.text: REAL ID adds no cost at renewal, but asking for it between renewals triggers the duplicate card fee.

teaching.text: Adding REAL ID at renewal is free; between renewals you pay the duplicate card fee. Remember: between renewals costs extra.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: REAL ID adds no cost at renewal, but asking for it between renewals triggers the duplicate card fee.

question.text: What proof should a newcomer bring when applying for a Michigan license?

answer.text: Newcomers from another state or country should apply for a Michigan license once residency is established, bringing proof of a Social Security number, of U.S. citizenship or legal presence, of identity and of Michigan residency.

teaching.text: Bring proof of your Social Security number, citizenship or legal presence, identity and Michigan residency. Remember: number, status, identity, address.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Newcomers from another state or country should apply for a Michigan license once residency is established, bringing proof of a Social Security number, of U.S. citizenship or legal presence, of identity and of Michigan residency.

question.text: After a newcomer's documents are approved, what tests or permits may follow?

answer.text: After your documents are approved a vision test is given, and a newcomer may also need the written knowledge test, a temporary instruction permit (TIP) and a driving skills test.

teaching.text: The vision test comes first, and some newcomers then need the knowledge test, a TIP and a skills test. Remember: vision first, then maybe more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After your documents are approved a vision test is given, and a newcomer may also need the written knowledge test, a temporary instruction permit (TIP) and a driving skills test.

question.text: Which licenses can be converted to a Michigan license without testing?

answer.text: A license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany or the Republic of Korea can be converted to a Michigan license without the knowledge test, TIP or skills test.

teaching.text: Valid licenses from another state, Canada, Germany or Korea convert with no knowledge test, TIP or skills test. Remember: states, Canada, Germany, Korea.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany or the Republic of Korea can be converted to a Michigan license without the knowledge test, TIP or skills test.

question.text: What must you do if your foreign license has expired or your out-of-state license lapsed long ago?

answer.text: Holding an expired foreign license, or an out-of-state license expired for at least four years, means you must get a TIP and pass a driving skills test before Michigan issues a license.

teaching.text: Expired foreign licenses, and out-of-state licenses expired four years or more, mean a TIP and a skills test. Remember: expired means permit and drive test.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Holding an expired foreign license, or an out-of-state license expired for at least four years, means you must get a TIP and pass a driving skills test before Michigan issues a license.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: expired means permit and drive test

question.text: What happens at the end of the application, and when does the license arrive?

answer.text: Your photo is taken and a fee set by license type and add-ons is charged, and the new Michigan license should arrive by mail in about three weeks.

teaching.text: After the photo and fee, the license is mailed and should arrive in about three weeks. Remember: photo, fee, mail.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Your photo is taken and a fee set by license type and add-ons is charged, and the new Michigan license should arrive by mail in about three weeks.

question.text: What are the three graduated license levels, and how are they issued?

answer.text: Graduated licenses, namely the Level one Learner’s, Level two Intermediate and Level three Full, are issued through Michigan’s driver education program for teens under eighteen.

teaching.text: Teens under eighteen move through Level one, Level two and Level three through driver education. Remember: learner, intermediate, full.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Graduated licenses, namely the Level one Learner’s, Level two Intermediate and Level three Full, are issued through Michigan’s driver education program for teens under eighteen.

question.text: What must applicants under eighteen complete, and who is excused?

answer.text: Applicants under eighteen must complete Graduated Driver Licensing, a step waived for anyone who has held a valid license from another state for more than a year.

teaching.text: Under-eighteen applicants complete GDL unless they held a valid out-of-state license for more than a year. Remember: teens go through GDL.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants under eighteen must complete Graduated Driver Licensing, a step waived for anyone who has held a valid license from another state for more than a year.

question.text: Which newcomers convert without testing, and which must get a permit and skills test?

answer.text: Licenses from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany or South Korea convert without testing, while an expired foreign license or an out-of-state license expired for at least four years sends you through a TIP and a skills test.

teaching.text: Valid licenses from the listed places convert; expired ones send you through a TIP and a skills test. Remember: valid converts, expired retests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Licenses from another U.S. state, Canada, Germany or South Korea convert without testing, while an expired foreign license or an out-of-state license expired for at least four years sends you through a TIP and a skills test.

question.text: When is the Graduated Driver Licensing requirement waived for an under-eighteen applicant?

answer.text: The Graduated Driver Licensing requirement for under-eighteen applicants is waived only when the teen has held a valid license from another state for more than a year.

teaching.text: The GDL waiver needs more than a year holding a valid license from another state. Remember: a year licensed elsewhere.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Graduated Driver Licensing requirement for under-eighteen applicants is waived only when the teen has held a valid license from another state for more than a year.
